children: The probability of a Federal Reserve rate increase next week has risen sharply after the latest producer price index came in firmer than expected.
Markets now assign a 69.8% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 FOMC meeting, up from 61.2% on Wednesday and just shy of 70%.

That repricing reflects growing concern that inflation remains too elevated for the central bank to stand pat. Traders quickly lifted the implied path of policy after the PPI data, treating the print as evidence that price pressures have not faded as much as hoped.
Treasury markets absorbed the shift immediately. The benchmark U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield
climbed 7 basis points to 4.92%, hovering just below 5% and reaching its highest level since the financial crisis.

Friday’s consumer price index report still looms as the next swing factor. A hot CPI reading could push hike odds even higher; a cooler one could pull them back. Until then, the message from this week’s PPI is clear: the odds of a September tightening have moved meaningfully higher, and bond yields have followed.
Wall Street is now watching whether the incoming inflation data confirms that shift or forces another reassessment before policymakers meet next week.

title: September Fed hike odds jump after the latest PPI inflation print
